# Commodity supercycle

Commodity prices move in swings of twenty to thirty years, far longer than the business cycle. The driver is the mismatch between demand, which can jump when a large economy industrialises, and supply, which takes a decade to respond.

## Mechanism

A demand shock meets mines and wells that were starved of investment during the previous slump. Prices rise for years. High prices pull in capital, new supply arrives late and all at once, and prices fall for years. See [[Capex cycle in mining]].

## Side effects

Exporting countries get a strong currency and a weak manufacturing base, which is worth its own note: [[Dutch disease]].

Background reading: [Kondratiev on long waves](Kondratiev%20waves.md).
